correctness.rationale: Read RESULT.md and source CHECKER.py. The hat-function Gram matrix satisfies 6G=J, with diagonal 2(a+b) and alternating off-diagonal lengths. After sign conjugation J is strictly diagonally dominant with an entrywise positive geometrically decaying inverse. The 2×2 Bloch determinant is c−d cosθ, c=3a²+8ab+3b²,d=2ab; the reciprocal Fourier coefficients are rho^{|k|}/sqrt(c²−d²). Its exact even/odd inverse yields alternating signs of kernel nodal entries, so absolute affine interpolation integrates via (u²+v²)/(2(u+v)). Geometric summation over four interval types and the root quadratic give the claimed rational norm. Convexity of x→∫|K(x,y)|dy between knots and reflection/translational symmetry yield global nodal maximum; symmetry yields L¹=L∞. Periodizing this integrable exponentially decaying kernel bounds all circles and gives convergence to the full-line norm. Independent exact rational inversion of 20 finite-circle Gram matrices (four (a,b) pairs and 5 repeat counts) confirmed all nodal absolute row integrals, strict finite bounds and trend. Infinite theorem rests on Bloch/periodization proof, not finite checks.

value.rationale: The period-two mesh is the simplest systematic nonuniform perturbation of uniform linear finite elements. A complete contrast law shows the surprising strict improvement of worst-case L∞ stability from 2 toward 5/3 as alternating knot lengths become uneven, and gives a sharp common envelope for all finite periodic-repeat counts. This is a motivated exact projection stability invariant.

final_claim: For positive alternating bi-infinite knot lengths a,b, the L²-orthogonal projector onto continuous affine splines extends to L¹ and L∞ with sharp equal norm (5a²+22ab+5b²)/(3a²+10ab+3b²)=2−(a−b)²/[(3a+b)(a+3b)]. On every 2m-knot periodic circle m≥2 the norm is at most this, and approaches it as m→∞.
limitations: Continuous degree-one orthogonal splines, alternating positive intervals only; no all-mesh optimal constant, higher degree or exact individual finite-m norm.
